title: Forgetting cyclic module coefficients reflects constancy
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $U$ an object of its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and $n\geq1$. Let $F$ be a sheaf of $\operatorname{ULift}(\mathbf Z/n)$-modules on the localized site $(Y_{\mathrm{et}})/U$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. If its underlying abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] is constant [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], then $F$ is constant as a module sheaf. No finiteness or nonemptiness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Definition 03RU (definition-finite-locally-constant), abelian and module clauses; Definition 03RW (definition-constructible) (2),(3). Agent-written cyclic-coefficient argument using the cokernel of multiplication by n.

proof.text: Let V forget cyclic module coefficients. Any additive map between V(P) and V(Q) is linear: write each lifted residue r as the image of an integer a, and use f(a x)=a f(x). Thus V is full and faithful, and so is its sheaf-composition functor. This is implemented by constructing a linear map from each additive map, then using the Mathlib fullness instances for sheafCompose.

Choose a constant abelian value E for the underlying sheaf G. Form Q=coker(n id_E). The cokernel projection is surjective; applying its zero-composition identity to y shows n times the image of y is zero, so nQ=0. Give Q the canonical Z/n-module action and restrict scalars along ULift.ringEquiv. No finiteness or point of the site is required.

The constant abelian sheaf functor L preserves cokernels, since it is a left adjoint (Mathlib constantSheafAdj, with the terminal object Over.mkIdTerminal). Every section of G is annihilated by n, using (n : ULift (ZMod n))=0. Conjugating through L(E) ≅ G gives L.map(n id_E)=0. Preservation of cokernels then identifies L(Q) with the cokernel of zero on L(E); in particular L.map(cokernel.π) is an isomorphism. These categorical calculations are explicitly proved using PreservesCokernel.π_iso_hom and cokernel.π_of_zero.

Constants commute with forgetting, so L(Q) is the underlying abelian sheaf of the constant cyclic module Q. Compose this comparison with G ≅ L(E) and the isomorphism L(E) ≅ L(Q). The full faithful sheaf-composition functor lifts this isomorphism back to cyclic module sheaves using preimageIso. Hence the original module sheaf is constant.
